data.title: ATF4 activates a transcriptional program that chronically suppresses mTOR activity and promotes neurodegeneration in Parkinson disease models
data.authors: Demmings MD; Kane EA; Tennyson EC; Hurley K; Zhao J; Cruickshanks NA; Ciz V; Krupa JM; Pasternak SH; Cregan SP

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Mouse (neurotoxin and alpha-synucleinopathy PD models) and cultured neurons
data.finding: Chronic integrated-stress-response signalling through ATF4 coordinately upregulates SESN2, DDIT4 and Trib3, which together suppress BOTH mTORC1 and mTORC2; this sustained mTOR inhibition drives dopaminergic neuron death via the pro-apoptotic BCL-2 family protein PUMA. Defines a maladaptive ISR/ATF4-to-mTOR axis in Parkinson disease models — a case where LESS mTOR activity is harmful, opposite to the usual longevity framing.
data.abstract_excerpt: The integrated stress response (ISR) enables cells to adapt to diverse cellular stresses, but during chronic or unresolved stress it becomes maladaptive and is implicated in neurodegenerative diseases, including Parkinson disease (PD). The mechanisms underlying maladaptive ISR-driven neurodegeneration, however, remain poorly defined. Here, we find a critical pathway by which chronic ISR activation promotes neurodegeneration in neurotoxin and alpha-synucleinopathy models of PD in vitro and in vivo.

extracted_findings.intervention: Chronic integrated stress response / ATF4 activation (neurotoxin and alpha-synuclein models)
extracted_findings.target: ATF4 -> SESN2, DDIT4, TRIB3 -> mTORC1 and mTORC2
extracted_findings.species: Mouse Parkinson disease models; cultured neurons
extracted_findings.effect: Sustained ATF4 signalling suppresses both mTOR complexes and drives dopaminergic neuron death via PUMA
